name: Housing
blurb: Kiến trúc, thuê mua, không gian sống

words.definitionEn: a place to live or stay
words.example: The city offers various types of accommodation for students.

words.definitionEn: features that make a place comfortable
words.example: The apartment complex has excellent amenities such as a pool and gym.

words.definitionEn: a person who designs buildings
words.example: The architect designed a sustainable house with solar panels.

words.definitionEn: the style of building
words.example: The architecture of the house is a blend of modern and traditional.

words.definitionEn: a platform projecting from the wall of a building
words.example: The balcony offers a stunning view of the city skyline.

words.definitionEn: the lowest floor of a building, partly or entirely below ground
words.example: The basement was converted into a home gym.

words.definitionEn: a room with glass walls and roof for plants or relaxation
words.example: They built a conservatory off the kitchen to enjoy natural light.

words.definitionEn: the process of building something
words.example: Construction of the new housing estate began last month.

words.definitionEn: a shared office environment for freelancers and remote workers
words.example: Many freelancers prefer to rent a co-working space for networking.

words.definitionEn: a small, cozy house, often in a rural area
words.example: They rented a cottage in the countryside for a weekend getaway.

words.definitionEn: the attractiveness of a property from the street
words.example: Improving curb appeal can significantly increase property value.

words.definitionEn: money paid upfront to secure a rental or purchase
words.example: The tenant paid a security deposit before moving in.

words.definitionEn: a house that is not attached to any other building
words.example: They prefer a detached house for more privacy.

words.definitionEn: a place where people live
words.example: The dwelling was poorly maintained and needed repairs.

words.definitionEn: using less energy to reduce costs and environmental impact
words.example: The house has energy-efficient windows and insulation.

words.definitionEn: a person who sells and rents properties
words.example: The estate agent showed us several houses in the area.

words.definitionEn: the outside of a building
words.example: The exterior of the building needs repainting after the storm.

words.definitionEn: the front of a building, often decorative
words.example: The facade was decorated with intricate ceramic tiles.

words.definitionEn: a diagram showing the layout of rooms in a building
words.example: The floor plan shows an open-plan living area and two bedrooms.

words.meaningVi: tịch thu nhà (vì không trả nợ)
words.definitionEn: to take possession of a property when the owner fails to repay a mortgage
words.example: The bank foreclosed on their home after six months of missed payments.

words.definitionEn: containing furniture such as beds, tables, and chairs
words.example: The apartment is fully furnished, so you can move in immediately.

words.meaningVi: khu dân cư có cổng bảo vệ
words.definitionEn: a residential area with a controlled entrance for security
words.example: They live in a gated community for safety and privacy.

words.meaningVi: sự chỉnh trang đô thị (làm tăng giá trị khu phố)
words.definitionEn: the process of renovating a neighborhood to attract wealthier residents
words.example: Gentrification often displaces long-term residents due to rising rents.

words.definitionEn: suitable for living in
words.example: The house is not habitable without major repairs to the roof.

words.definitionEn: a tall building with many floors
words.example: The high-rise offers panoramic views of the entire city.

words.definitionEn: the state of owning a home
words.example: The government introduces policies to promote homeownership among young people.

words.definitionEn: basic facilities needed for a society to function, such as roads and utilities
words.example: The area lacks adequate infrastructure for public transport.

words.definitionEn: the inside of a building
words.example: The interior was decorated with taste and attention to detail.

words.definitionEn: a person who owns and rents out property
words.example: The landlord increased the rent without notice.

words.definitionEn: a contract specifying the terms of renting a property
words.example: They signed a one-year lease with an option to renew.

words.meaningVi: gác xép, căn hộ áp mái
words.definitionEn: a large, open room under a roof, often converted into a living space
words.example: The loft was converted into a studio apartment.

words.definitionEn: the process of keeping a property in good condition
words.example: Regular maintenance is essential to avoid costly repairs.

words.definitionEn: a loan from a bank to buy a property
words.example: They took out a mortgage to buy a house in the suburbs.

words.definitionEn: a district or community within a larger city
words.example: The neighbourhood is very quiet and family-friendly.

words.definitionEn: the act of living in or using a property
words.example: The occupancy rate of the building has increased recently.

words.definitionEn: having few internal walls to create a spacious feel
words.example: The open-plan kitchen and living room are ideal for entertaining.

words.meaningVi: căn hộ áp mái cao cấp
words.definitionEn: an apartment on the top floor of a building, often luxurious
words.example: The penthouse has a private terrace and stunning views.

words.definitionEn: a building or land owned by someone
words.example: The property is worth a lot after renovation.

words.definitionEn: the act of restoring or improving a building
words.example: The renovation took three months and cost a fortune.

words.definitionEn: to pay to live in a property owned by someone else
words.example: They rent an apartment in the city center.

words.definitionEn: relating to renting a property
words.example: The rental market is highly competitive in this city.

words.definitionEn: a place where someone lives
words.example: The residence is near the park and has a garden.

words.definitionEn: suitable for living in, rather than business
words.example: The area is mainly residential with few shops.

words.definitionEn: money held by the landlord to cover damages
words.example: They paid a security deposit when moving in, which was refunded later.

words.definitionEn: attached to another house on one side
words.example: They live in a semi-detached house with a shared wall.

words.definitionEn: a very tall building with many floors
words.example: The city skyline is filled with skyscrapers of glass and steel.

words.definitionEn: a one-room apartment with a combined living and sleeping area
words.example: She lives in a small studio in the university district.

words.definitionEn: relating to a suburb, a residential area outside a city
words.example: They prefer suburban living for its peace and quiet.

words.definitionEn: a person who rents a property from a landlord
words.example: The tenant complained about the lack of hot water.

words.definitionEn: the regulation of land use by local authorities
words.example: Zoning laws restrict the construction of tall buildings in residential areas.
